difficulty_reason: The lemma is the base change permanence of the relative notion of finite presentation of the same section: if M is an A-module finitely presented relative to R and R to R' is an arbitrary ring map, then the base changed module M tensor over R with R' is finitely presented relative to R' (statement lines 21047-21055). The proof is a 13-line presentation (proof lines 21058-21070): it chooses a surjection from a polynomial ring over R onto A and a presentation matrix for M over that polynomial ring, tensors the whole presentation with R', and observes that a presentation over a polynomial ring over R remains a presentation over the polynomial ring over R' with the same number of generators and relations. The point that makes the argument short is that the base change of R[x_1, ..., x_n] is R'[x_1, ..., x_n] and that tensoring with R' is right exact, so nothing has to be added to the presentation; this is exactly why the relative notion is base change stable while the absolute notion is not.
